reason: Collector, M7C, M9V, M9Y, M10B and M10E persistent loops use exclusive lock files that are normally removed on graceful process exit. A Windows forced reboot/power loss can leave those lock files behind even though no loop process remains.

recovery_behavior.first_check: Confirm no protected collector/M7C/M9V/M9Y/M10B/M10E loop process is running by Windows process command line.
recovery_behavior.if_stale_lock_exists_and_no_loop_running: Archive the lock under LOCALAPPDATA reboot_recovery timestamp folder, then remove only that stale lock.

restart_order_after_recovery_pass: Confirm MT5 terminal / CSV exporter is running and goldsharp/btcusdsharp CSVs resume updating.
never_after_reboot: Do not rerun/reset the M7C prospective runtime initializer.
Do not rerun/reset the M8C prospective initializer/start.
Do not rerun M9V BAT00 or BAT01.
Do not delete runtime manifests/start receipts manually.
Do not backfill by changing a frozen prospective start.
data_gap_note: Persistent scripts can reconstruct reports from frozen starts and currently available source data only. Cloudflare can catch up from its preserved cursor/database. MT5 raw CSVs must actually contain/restore missed CLOSED bars after terminal restart. If an MT5 CSV has a permanent gap, that interval is unobserved forward time for M9V/M9Y/M10B/M10E and must not be silently counted, interpolated, or reconstructed using later outcomes.
